assessment.nobel_worthiness: Mapping the acoustic peaks and then the full-sky anisotropy of the CMB turned cosmology into a precision science and fixed the content of the universe: ordinary matter, dark matter and dark energy. This is a discovery read directly from nature, and it is the empirical foundation for every dark-energy discussion I care about. The 2006 COBE prize and the 2019 prize for theoretical cosmology did not cover this precision mapping.
assessment.attribution: The WMAP trio of Bennett (PI), Page (instrument and experiment) and Spergel (analysis and cosmological parameters) is a coherent configuration. Puget (Planck/HFI) and Sunyaev (theory of CMB physics and the SZ effect) have strong claims, and omitting them, along with the balloon experiments that first resolved the peaks, is a real allocation problem that the full committee would need to discuss.
assessment.maturity: Very mature: WMAP and Planck are independent, mutually consistent, and the interpretation (LCDM) has been stable for two decades. Recognition is not premature and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Whether a three-person split can fairly exclude Planck leadership, Sunyaev and the early balloon experiments.
The Hubble-constant tension and other anomalies do not undermine the CMB result itself, but may colour how the committee frames the citation.
I am relying on my own recollection of the roles of the named individuals and have not verified them independently.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Direct, horizon-scale images of M87* and Sgr A* give observational access to strong-field gravity and the black-hole shadow. The existential dimension is considerable, and for someone who has worked on black holes and horizonless mimickers it is exactly the type of clue from nature that theory needs. The result confirms the shadow size predicted by general relativity at the current precision.
assessment.attribution: Falcke (the 2000 shadow proposal and the BlackHoleCam push), Doeleman (EHT founding director, VLBI at 1.3 mm) and Zensus (MPIfR and EHT board, VLBI leadership) are defensible, but the collaboration was very large and several essential figures (for example VLBI pioneers and the data-calibration and imaging leads) would be omitted. Credit remains contested.
assessment.maturity: Fairly mature: 2019 M87* result, 2022 Sgr A*, and multi-year polarization and variability follow-ups. Independent confirmation by a second array or at higher frequency is still limited, and the interpretation of the ring as a pure GR shadow has tolerances that leave room for alternatives.
uncertainties: Collaboration-scale credit and the three-person limit.
The precision of the GR test is modest, so the discovery is imaging, not yet a decisive test of horizons versus mimickers.
Roles of named individuals recalled from memory, not verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Detection of a diffuse flux of astrophysical neutrinos at TeV-PeV energies, then a point source (TXS 0506+056 and NGC 1068), opened neutrino astronomy and addressed the origin of cosmic rays. The instrument, a cubic kilometre of Antarctic ice, was a bold idea that paid off. This is a discovery built on a measurement and not on speculation.
assessment.attribution: Halzen is the central intellectual and project driver of IceCube and its precursor AMANDA, and Karle is a leading figure in the detector and ice-physics development. Since only two names are credited, a three-person configuration would need a third name that is not supplied; DeYoung, Ahrens, or earlier pioneers are not available to me here, and I flag the gap.
assessment.maturity: Mature enough: IceCube observations are internally cross-checked, and KM3NeT and Baikal-GVD provide growing independent corroboration. The point-source identifications are more recent, but the diffuse flux is firm.
uncertainties: Whether two names fairly represent a large collaboration.
The origin of the diffuse flux is not fully settled.
Earlier pioneers of deep-water or ice neutrino detection are not on the credited list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theoretical prediction of flat bands at the magic angle and the experimental observation of correlated insulating and superconducting phases in twisted bilayer graphene created a new platform for correlated physics. It is a clean case where a theory prediction, unlike many I distrust, was confirmed by experiment, and it spawned a field of moire materials.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the key 2011 prediction; Jarillo-Herrero's group delivered the 2018 experimental observation. This is a natural theory-plus-experiment trio. Cao and Fatemi, who were the experimental lead authors, and others who contributed (for example the Dean and Young groups, Kim) are not on the list, so credit disputes may remain.
assessment.maturity: Moderately mature: reproduced by many groups with different substrates and twist architectures, but the origin of superconductivity and some of the correlated states is still being debated, and the field is just eight years old.
uncertainties: Premature relative to the long-term significance for applications and for the pairing mechanism.
Role of junior experimentalists and competing groups.
Details of the credit chain recalled from memory.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery of superconductivity at 26 K and then up to 55 K in iron pnictides was a surprise that opened a second family of high-Tc superconductors and broke the idea that copper oxides were unique. The results are experimental clues from nature, which is where I think progress comes from.
assessment.attribution: Attribution is unusually clear: Hosono and collaborators (including Kamihara) made the 2008 discovery. A single laureate is a valid configuration, though some may feel that Chinese groups rapidly extended Tc to 55 K, and that this subsequent work deserves acknowledgement.
assessment.maturity: Mature: independently confirmed within weeks and extensively studied for more than fifteen years. The theory of pairing is still unresolved, which could be either a reason to wait or no obstacle for a discovery prize.
uncertainties: Whether the unresolved mechanism and lack of technological payoff weigh against it.
Role of co-authors such as Kamihara and the rapid Chinese follow-up work.
Prior Nobel recognition of cuprate superconductivity may be seen as overlapping.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Katori's magic-wavelength optical lattice proposal and Ye's demonstration of record-level stability and systematics control made optical lattice clocks the most precise instruments ever built. They enable tests of fundamental constants and relativistic redshift at millimetre scale, and eventually a redefinition of the second.
assessment.attribution: Katori invented the concept and Ye led its precision realization; this is a clean two-person attribution. Other lattice-clock groups (Lemke, Ludlow, Hinkley, Bloom) contributed, and the NIST/JILA program benefited from Hall and Hänsch, who already hold a prize.
assessment.maturity: Mature: independent clocks around the world agree at the 10^-18 level, though the redefinition of the second has not yet occurred, which may make some members think recognition premature.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2005 and 2012 prizes in precision metrology, and with ion-clock work.
The pending redefinition of the second.
Whether this counts as fundamental physics or an instrument.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery of millisecond radio bursts of extragalactic origin, followed by their cosmological use and the CHIME repeaters, opened a new window on the universe, and the Galactic magnetar burst linked at least some to compact objects. It is a discovery that was found in archival data by clues in nature, which fits my sense of how physics advances.
assessment.attribution: The 2007 Lorimer burst paper credits Lorimer, McLaughlin and Bailes (with Narkevic and Crawford). The more recent CHIME and ASKAP localizations (for example Bannister, Shannon, Ravi and the CHIME team) form a significant part of the story, and the exclusion of those groups would be debated.
assessment.maturity: Mid maturity: the population and extragalactic nature are established by many independent telescopes, but the emission mechanism and progenitors remain largely unknown, making the discovery stable and the interpretation open.
uncertainties: Progenitor and emission mechanism are not settled.
Whether early skepticism (the Perytons) and later confirmation by Thornton et al. should affect the credit.
Credit roles recalled from memory.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery of 1992 QB1 revealed the Kuiper Belt, transformed our picture of the outer Solar System, and led to the reclassification of Pluto. It has an existential dimension, since it tells us how our planetary system formed and relates to debris disks around other stars.
assessment.attribution: Two names that both credibly made the discovery of the first object together, which makes a clean allocation. Earlier theoretical predictions (Edgeworth, Kuiper, Fernandez) are historic and the dynamical interpretation could invite additional names, but those are not on the supplied list.
assessment.maturity: Very mature: thousands of Kuiper Belt Objects have been found and the structure is well characterized. Recognition is long-timed, but the field may be considered planetary science and not physics.
uncertainties: Whether the Physics prize is the right home for a planetary-science discovery.
Earlier theoretical predictions of a trans-Neptunian population.
Competing claims about the order of discovery are not evaluated here.
